q: The phase of plant growth marked by active cell division with small, thin-walled cells is the:
why: Meristematic cells divide actively by mitosis and are small with dense cytoplasm.

q: When growth is plotted against time, plants typically show a curve of the shape:
why: Growth shows lag, log and stationary phases, giving a sigmoid curve.

q: Which plant hormone is best known for promoting apical dominance and cell elongation?
why: Auxins (e.g. IAA) promote cell elongation and suppress lateral bud growth (apical dominance).

q: Spraying GA3 (gibberellin) on sugarcane mainly increases:
why: Gibberellins promote stem/internode elongation, increasing crop height.

q: A hormone that promotes fruit ripening and leaf abscission is:
why: Ethylene is the gaseous hormone responsible for ripening and abscission.

q: A chrysanthemum that flowers only when day length is less than a critical value is classified as a:
why: Short day plants flower when day length falls below a critical value, e.g. chrysanthemum.

q: Winter wheat flowering earlier after cold treatment of seeds is an example of:
why: Vernalization is flowering promotion through exposure to low temperature.

q: Which of the following is classified as a plant micronutrient (needed in trace amounts)?
why: Iron is a micronutrient needed in trace amounts, unlike the macronutrients N, K, Ca.

q: Interveinal chlorosis in leaves is a classic deficiency symptom of which element, since it is part of the chlorophyll molecule?
why: Magnesium is a core component of chlorophyll; its deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis.

q: Biological nitrogen fixation, converting N2 to NH3, is catalysed by the enzyme:
why: The enzyme nitrogenase (in Rhizobium/Azotobacter) converts atmospheric N2 into ammonia.
